topic: The Trinity of Logic: Ternary, Towers, and Triangles
target_audience: Undergraduate Computer Science or Mathematics students

outline.topic: The Trinity of Logic: Ternary, Towers, and Triangles
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate Computer Science or Mathematics students

sections.title: Foundation: The Power of Three (Ternary)
sections.content: Introduce the Base-3 (ternary) counting system. Explain how each digit represents a state (0, 1, or 2) and how position indicates magnitude ($3^0, 3^1, 3^2$). This serves as the 'coordinate system' for the entire lesson.
sections.example: Visualize a 3-state light switch: 'Off' (0), 'Dim' (1), and 'Bright' (2). Counting from 0 to 8 in ternary (000 to 222) represents all possible configurations of 3 such switches.

sections.title: The Rule Change: Constrained Towers of Hanoi
sections.content: Introduce the 'Linear' or 'Constrained' Towers of Hanoi. Unlike the classic version, disks can only move between ADJACENT pegs (Peg 0 ↔ Peg 1 ↔ Peg 2). To move from Peg 0 to Peg 2, a disk must stop at Peg 1 first. This constraint forces a specific, recursive path.
sections.example: Imagine three rooms in a line (Living Room, Hallway, Bedroom). You cannot teleport a heavy sofa from the Living Room to the Bedroom; it must pass through the Hallway.

sections.title: Mapping States to Geometry
sections.content: Define a 'State' as the position of $n$ disks. Represent every possible valid configuration of disks as a vertex (dot) on a graph. Connect vertices with lines if a single legal move can transition one state to another. This transforms a logic puzzle into a geometric map.
sections.example: With 1 disk, the map is a simple line: State [0]—[1]—[2]. With 2 disks, the map starts to branch, forming small triangles.

sections.title: Emergence of the Sierpinski Triangle
sections.content: Demonstrate that as the number of disks ($n$) increases, the state-space graph of the constrained Hanoi puzzle perfectly forms a Sierpinski Triangle. Each larger triangle is composed of three smaller versions of itself, representing the placement of the largest disk on Peg 0, 1, or 2.
sections.example: Zoom out from a 1-disk line to a 3-disk fractal. Show that the 'corners' of the Sierpinski Triangle represent all disks stacked on a single peg (000, 111, or 222 in ternary).

sections.title: Fractal Traversal via Ternary Addresses
sections.content: Synthesize the concepts. Show how a ternary number acts as a 'GPS address' to find any state on the Sierpinski Triangle. Traversing the edges of the triangle is equivalent to solving the puzzle. The longest path (from Peg 0 to Peg 2) follows the outer boundary of the fractal.
sections.example: A digital ant needs to move from the 'All-on-0' corner to the 'All-on-2' corner. By following the ternary sequence (000 → 001 → ... → 222), the ant traces the zig-zag perimeter of the Sierpinski gasket.

storyboard.title: Foundation: The Power of Three (Ternary)
lecture_lines: Binary uses two states, but ternary uses three.
Ternary digits represent states zero, one, and two.
Positional values are powers of three: one, three, nine.
Three-state switches generate twenty-seven unique configurations.
This base-3 system coordinates our entire logical map.
animations: Fade in the title 'The Power of Three (Ternary)' in #FFFFFF at the top center.
Display three circles labeled 0, 1, and 2. Sequentially highlight 0 in #00FF00, 1 in #FFFF00, and 2 in #FF0000.
Show magnitude labels: 3^2, 3^1, and 3^0 in #00FFFF arranged horizontally.
Place digits '2', '1', and '0' under labels. Show the calculation 2*9 + 1*3 + 0*1.
Transform the ternary digits into decimal '21' and flash it in #FFFFFF.

storyboard.title: The Rule Change: Constrained Towers of Hanoi
lecture_lines: Classic Hanoi allows moves between any two pegs.
We restrict moves to adjacent pegs only.
Moving from peg zero to two requires intermediate steps.
This constraint creates a specific, predictable recursive path.
Every legal transition follows this strict linear rule.
animations: Show three vertical pegs labeled 0, 1, and 2 in #FFFFFF. Place an orange disk (#FF8C00) on Peg 0.
Draw a red 'X' (#FF0000) over the direct path from Peg 0 to Peg 2 to show it is forbidden.
Animate the disk moving from Peg 0 to Peg 1, then from Peg 1 to Peg 2, following green arrows (#00FF00).

storyboard.title: Mapping States to Geometry
lecture_lines: Every valid disk configuration is a graph vertex.
Lines connect states reachable by one legal move.
One disk creates a simple line of three states.
animations: Plot 3 dots in a horizontal line (#00FFFF) labeled 0, 1, and 2. Connect with white lines.
Arrange 3 copies of this line into a triangular formation. Label groups by Disk 2's position.
Draw white edges connecting the corners of these three groups to form a larger triangle.
Highlight a specific vertex and display the corresponding disk configuration on pegs in a small window.
Fade out labels and highlight the resulting 9-vertex graph structure in #FFFFFF.

storyboard.title: Emergence of the Sierpinski Triangle
lecture_lines: Adding more disks expands the state-space graph recursively.
Two disks form three connected triangles of states.
Increasing disks reveals the iconic Sierpinski Triangle fractal.
Corners represent all disks stacked on a single peg.
The fractal structure perfectly captures the game's logic.
animations: Scale down the 9-vertex graph and triplicate it to construct the 3-disk state space.
Connect the three groups with new edges to complete the Sierpinski Triangle in #FFD700.
Label the three outermost corners as '000', '111', and '222' in #FF00FF.
Zoom into one corner to show the self-similar recursive structure within the fractal.
Pan out to reveal the full 27-state Sierpinski gasket representing 3 disks.

storyboard.title: Fractal Traversal via Ternary Addresses
lecture_lines: Ternary numbers act as addresses for every puzzle state.
Solving the puzzle means traversing the fractal's edges.
The longest path follows the triangle's outer perimeter.
animations: Trace a bold green path (#00FF00) from corner '000' to corner '222' along the fractal boundary.
Update a ternary counter on screen from 000 to 222 as the path progress.
Display the text 'Puzzle Solved' in #FFFFFF as the path reaches the final corner.
